mainTopic: יוצא דופן and the animal born after it: is a 'בכור לדבר אחד' a בכור? The ברייתא that defines a בכור from the פסוקים, and אביי's and רבינא's ways of reading it.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion, which explains why two cases both had to be taught. Then a new משנה brings an animal born by יוצא דופן (caesarean birth) and the animal born naturally after it. רבי טרפון treats both as doubtful בכורות, and רבי עקיבא says neither is a בכור. The גמרא explains that they argue about a 'בכור לדבר אחד', an animal that is a firstborn in only one way. A ברייתא then defines a בכור from three words in the פסוקים: 'זכר', 'פטר רחם' and 'בכור'. Each word fills a gap left by the others. רב שרביא challenges the ברייתא, because its first half seems to say a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is a בכור and its second half seems to say it is not. אביי answers that it is not a בכור by reading the first half as being about the caesarean animal itself. רבינא answers that it is a בכור, and that the second half learns its lesson from the word 'בכור' being extra.

steps.title: Why both cases had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. Both cases were needed, because otherwise we might have thought the offspring of the mother that had not given birth before is the better one.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that this one, born to the mother that had not given birth before, is better. So it was necessary to teach both cases.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion from the previous page. The גמרא is wrapping up its explanation of why two similar cases both had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked why it needed to teach two cases that look alike. It answers that without the second case, we might have assumed the offspring of the mother that 'had not given birth before' is the better animal. Since that mistake was possible, each case needed to be stated on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: she had already given birth before (she had 'made a firstborn')
better, superior
more
it was necessary (to teach both cases)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new topic. It is the end of an argument that began on the previous page, so don't look for its question here.

phrases.english: that this one, of the mother that had not given birth before,
phrases.notes: The first half of this sentence is on the previous page. It finishes a thought: 'you might have said that…'

phrases.english: is better. So it was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a צריכותא discussion carried over from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases had to be taught, because without one of them we could have wrongly assumed the offspring of the mother that had not given birth before is superior.

steps.title: Caesarean birth and the animal after it: רבי טרפון's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents an animal born by יוצא דופן and the one born naturally after it. רבי טרפון says both must graze until they get a מום, and then the owner may eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An animal born by caesarean, and the one that comes after it: רבי טרפון says both of them graze until they become blemished, and then they are eaten in their blemished state by the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case where the first animal was born by caesarean and a second animal was born after it the normal way. רבי טרפון says both are treated as doubtful בכורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal has one 'firstborn' quality but is missing the other. The first was born first but did not open the womb. The second opened the womb but was not born first. Because רבי טרפון is unsure about them, neither can be treated as a regular animal, and neither can be treated as a sure בכור. So they wait until they get a מום, and then the owner eats them.

keyTerms.meaning: born through the side (caesarean birth)
they shall graze (be left out to pasture)
until they become blemished and unfit as קרבנות
in their blemished state
to the owners (not to the כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: Being eaten by the owner does not mean רבי טרפון says they are definitely not בכורות. He is unsure, so he treats them strictly in some ways (no work or regular use until a מום) and leniently in others (the owner keeps them).

phrases.english: Mishnah: An animal born through the side
phrases.notes: This means a caesarean birth: the animal came out through a cut in the mother's side, not through the womb's opening.

phrases.english: and the one that comes after it,
Rabbi Tarfon says:
both of them graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, both the caesarean-born animal and the one after it graze until they get a מום, and then the owner eats them.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: neither animal is a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says neither animal is a בכור. The first did not open the womb, and the second was preceded by another animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: neither of them is a בכור. The first, because it is not 'פטר רחם'. The second, because another one came before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי טרפון. He says both animals are completely regular, non-בכור animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives a separate reason for each animal. The first fails because the תורה describes a בכור as 'פטר רחם', the one that opens the womb, and this animal did not. The second fails because it was not the first animal born to its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: the one that opens the womb (the תורה's description of a בכור)
another one came before it
firstborn animal, which has קדושה and goes to the כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
neither of them is a firstborn;
the first, because it is not 'the one that opens the womb',
phrases.notes: This quotes the פסוק in שמות that describes a בכור as the one that opens the womb.

phrases.english: and the second, because another one came before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶן אֵינָן בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי טרפון in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, neither animal is a בכור: the first did not open the womb, and the second was not born first.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the underlying reason behind the argument in the משנה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים look at the same facts. The גמרא wants to find the one idea that makes רבי טרפון unsure while רבי עקיבא is certain.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: Gemara: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רבי טרפון from רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: A firstborn in only one way
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון is unsure whether a 'בכור לדבר אחד' (a firstborn in only one way) counts as a בכור. רבי עקיבא is sure it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון is in doubt: something that is a firstborn in one way, is it a בכור or not? And רבי עקיבא holds it is obvious: a firstborn in one way is not a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two תנאים argue about how to treat an animal that has only one of the two 'firstborn' qualities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal in the משנה is a 'בכור לדבר אחד'. The first was born first, and the second opened the womb. רבי טרפון is unsure whether one quality is enough, so he treats both as doubtful. רבי עקיבא holds that both qualities are needed, so neither animal is a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn in only one respect
he is in doubt about it
it is obvious to him

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה depends on 'בכור לדבר אחד'. רבי טרפון has a ספק about it, so both animals are doubtful. רבי עקיבא holds it is not a בכור, so both animals are regular.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea explains the whole משנה, and the ברייתא that follows starts defining exactly what a real בכור needs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon is in doubt:
a firstborn in one respect,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָוֵי בְּכוֹר אִי לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: whether it is a firstborn or is not a firstborn,
and to Rabbi Akiva it is obvious:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: a firstborn in one respect is not a firstborn.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about a 'בכור לדבר אחד'. רבי טרפון is unsure whether it is a בכור, and רבי עקיבא is sure it is not.

steps.title: A ברייתא introduces the method of general and specific
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא introduces the method of learning called 'מכלל הצריך לפרט ומפרט הצריך לכלל' and asks how it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: from a general statement that needs a specific detail, and from a specific detail that needs a general statement. How does this work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that will define a בכור from the פסוקים. This line only names the method, setting up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this method, the general word and the specific word each need the other to give the full meaning. The general word alone would include too much, and the detail alone would include too little. The ברייתא now shows how this works for the word 'בכור'.

keyTerms.meaning: a general statement
a specific detail
how so?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the usual 'כלל ופרט' rule, which limits the general word to the detail. Here the general word and the detail each explain the other.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
from a general statement that needs a detail
and from a detail that needs a general statement. How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that defines a בכור from the פסוקים, after the discussion about what counts as a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The definition of a בכור is learned through 'מכלל הצריך לפרט ומפרט הצריך לכלל'.

steps.title: Only a male is a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The general word 'כל בכור' might have included a female. The detail 'זכר' teaches that only a male is a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn.' I might think even a female is included. So the פסוק says 'male'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its first example. The general word 'בכור' could have included females, so the detail 'זכר' limits it to males.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כלל 'קדש לי כל בכור' alone would make every first offspring a בכור, even a female. The פרט 'זכר' narrows this to males only. This is the first step in building the full definition of a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn' (שמות יג:ב)
I might have thought
included in the meaning
therefore the פסוק says
male

phrases.english: 'Sanctify to Me every firstborn,'
phrases.notes: This is the general statement, the כלל, from שמות.

phrases.english: I might think even a female is included?
Therefore the verse says 'male.'
phrases.notes: This word comes from a פסוק in דברים about every firstborn male. It is the detail, the פרט.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״קַדֶּשׁ לִי כׇל בְּכוֹר״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נְקֵבָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first example of the method introduced in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female is not a בכור. The detail 'זכר' limits the general word 'בכור' to males.

steps.title: Male alone is not enough, so the verse adds 'opens the womb'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If we only had 'זכר', a male born after a female might count. So the פסוק adds 'פטר רחם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse said only 'male,' you might think a male is a בכור even if a female was born before it. So the verse says 'that which opens the womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with its method of each word filling a gap. Now it shows why 'זכר' alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זכר' tells us only males count, but it does not tell us the male must be the first to come out. A male born after a female did not open the womb, so 'פטר רחם' is needed to rule him out.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a possible wrong conclusion)
A female animal
Therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)
That which opens the womb, the first to come out of the mother

phrases.english: If the verse said only 'male,' one might think
that it counts even if a female came out before it?
So the verse teaches: 'that which opens the womb.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״זָכָר״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's chain of words, each one filling a gap left by the one before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A male born after a female is not a בכור, because he did not open the womb.

steps.title: 'Opens the womb' alone is not enough, so the verse adds 'firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: If we only had 'פטר רחם', an animal born naturally after an older sibling born by caesarean might count. So the פסוק adds 'בכור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse said only 'opens the womb,' you might think an animal counts even if it came out after an older sibling born by caesarean. So the verse says 'firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its chain. It shows why 'פטר רחם' alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born naturally after a caesarean sibling really did open the womb. But it was not the first one born, so the word 'בכור' is needed to rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born through the side, by caesarean section
Firstborn, the first one born

steps.confusionAlert: 'יצא אחר יוצא דופן' does NOT mean the caesarean animal itself. It means the second animal, which was born the normal way after its older sibling came out by caesarean.

phrases.english: If the verse said only 'opens the womb,' one might think
that it counts even if it came out after one born by caesarean?
So the verse teaches: 'firstborn.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצָא אַחַר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal born after a caesarean sibling is not a בכור, because it was not born first.

steps.title: The two halves of the ברייתא seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא tells אביי that the first half of the ברייתא suggests a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is a בכור, while the second half suggests it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said to אביי: In the first part, the ברייתא does not use the word 'firstborn' to rule out the male born after a female. That suggests a firstborn in one way counts as a firstborn. In the second part, it does use 'firstborn' to rule out the animal born after a caesarean. That suggests a firstborn in one way does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא challenges the ברייתא as contradicting itself. He connects it to the question of a 'בכור לדבר אחד' from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male born after a female is the first male, which makes him a 'firstborn in one way.' If 'בכור' could rule him out, the ברייתא would have used it, so it seems he IS called a בכור. In the second part the ברייתא does use 'בכור' to rule out a 'firstborn in one way' (the first to open the womb), so it seems he is NOT called a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching
Brings, cites (as the source)
So it seems, this shows that
A firstborn in only one way

phrases.english: רב שרביא said to אביי:
In the first part, the ברייתא does not cite 'firstborn' as the source,
phrases.notes: He means the male born after a female, which the ברייתא ruled out with 'opens the womb' instead.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.
phrases.english: so it seems a firstborn in one way is a firstborn.
In the last part, the ברייתא does cite 'firstborn' as the source,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר!
phrases.english: so it seems a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא לְאַבָּיֵי: רֵישָׁא לָא קָנָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא ״בְּכוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted in light of the 'בכור לדבר אחד' question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא on 'בכור לדבר אחד'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The way the first part chooses its sources implies one rule, and the way the last part chooses its sources implies the opposite rule.

steps.title: אביי: it is not a בכור, and the first part is about the caesarean animal itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is not a בכור. He explains that the first part is really ruling out the caesarean animal itself, which only 'פטר רחם' can exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי answered: Really, a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn. The first part means this: If the verse said only 'male,' you might think even an animal born by caesarean counts. So the verse says 'opens the womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He keeps the second part as it is and reads the first part in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born by caesarean really was born first, so the word 'בכור' cannot rule it out. Only 'פטר רחם' can, which is why the first part uses that phrase. Once 'פטר רחם' is there, it also rules out a male born after a female, so the first part's choice of source says nothing about the 'בכור לדבר אחד' question.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeping the original position)
This is what it means

phrases.english: He said to him: Really,

phrases.aramaic: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: a firstborn in one way is not a firstborn,
and this is what the first part means:

phrases.aramaic: אִי זָכָר, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן?
phrases.english: If the verse said only 'male,' one might think even one born by caesarean counts?
So the verse teaches: 'opens the womb.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the first part of the ברייתא (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first part was ruling out a male born after a female, which suggested that 'בכור' could not do that job.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is ruling out the caesarean animal itself, which 'בכור' truly cannot exclude, so no contradiction remains.

steps.title: רבינא: it is a בכור, and the last part learns from the extra word
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is a בכור. He explains that the last part learns from the fact that the word 'בכור' would otherwise be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, a firstborn in one way is a firstborn. The last part means this: If you think the animal born after a caesarean sibling is holy, why do I need the word 'firstborn' that the תורה wrote?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer to the contradiction. He keeps the first part as it is and reads the last part in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By its plain meaning, 'בכור' would include a firstborn in one way. But the other words already cover everything else, so 'בכור' would serve no purpose. That extra word is what excludes the animal born after a caesarean.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you were to think
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Why do I need it? (this word seems extra)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is not a בכור, and the first part is about the caesarean animal itself. רבינא: it is a בכור, and the word 'בכור' excludes only because it is extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers keep the ברייתא's ruling that the animal born after a caesarean sibling is not a בכור. They differ only on why: for אביי it comes from what 'בכור' means, and for רבינא it comes from the word being extra.

phrases.english: רבינא said: Really,
a firstborn in one way is a firstborn,
and this is what the last part means:
If it enters your mind
that one that came out after one born by caesarean is holy,
why do I need the word 'firstborn' that the Torah wrote?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, opposite way to answer רב שרביא's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the last part of the ברייתא as a lesson from an extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last part used the plain meaning of 'בכור' to exclude, which suggested that a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is not a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last part excludes only because 'בכור' would otherwise be unnecessary, so the first part's implication that a 'בכור לדבר אחד' is a בכור still stands.
